past_medical_history: B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia (B-ALL) — diagnosed 3 months ago; currently receiving induction chemotherapy

social_history.living_situation: Lives with wife and two children

neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: Intact. No facial weakness. No ptosis. Gag preserved.
neurological_exam.motor: Pure motor quadriplegia with rapid progression: upper limb power grade 3/5 bilaterally. Lower limb power grade 0/5 — cannot lift legs at all. No sensory deficits.
neurological_exam.sensory: Intact sensation to light touch, pinprick, vibration in all extremities — PURE MOTOR syndrome.
neurological_exam.reflexes: Complete global areflexia — absent bilaterally all extremities.
neurological_exam.coordination: Cannot assess lower limbs. Upper limb coordination impaired by weakness.
neurological_exam.additional: FVC: 2.8 L (predicted 4.2 L — 67%). NIF: -34 cmH2O. Bladder function intact. Respiratory function intact. Onset: 48-hour rapid progression, 3 days after 4th vincristine dose. No preceding infection identified. CSF: no blasts (last assessment). Pure motor syndrome with intact sensation — atypical for classic GBS but typical for AMAN variant.

patient.chief_complaint: Forty-eight-hour rapidly progressive ascending quadriplegia in ALL patient 3 days after fourth vincristine dose — pure motor with intact sensation.
patient.history_present_illness: Mr. M. is a 38-year-old man with B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia who is currently in week 4 of induction chemotherapy per a MRC-based protocol including vincristine, daunorubicin, prednisone, and L-asparaginase. He received his fourth weekly vincristine dose 3 days ago. Over the past 48 hours he has developed rapidly progressive weakness of all four limbs. He first noted bilateral leg weakness, and over the following 24 hours the weakness ascended to involve both arms. He is now unable to lift his legs off the bed. He has no sensory symptoms whatsoever — sensation is completely intact throughout. He has no dysphagia, no diplopia, no ptosis, and no facial weakness. Bladder and bowel function are preserved. There was no preceding diarrheal illness, respiratory infection, or viral prodrome prior to the vincristine dose. His leukocytosis (14,300/mm³) and thrombocytopenia (98,700/mm³) are expected findings from his ALL and induction chemotherapy. The differential is immediately dominated by two competing diagnoses: vincristine-induced neuropathy (known complication of this agent) versus acute motor axonal neuropathy (AMAN) variant of GBS. Vincristine typically causes a sensory-predominant 'dying-back' neuropathy with paresthesias and sensory loss first — the pure motor syndrome without any sensory involvement here argues against vincristine as the primary cause. The 48-hour rapid progression and global areflexia also favor GBS over the more insidious vincristine neuropathy timeline.

quantitative_data.pattern: Pure motor axonal polyradiculoneuropathy. Lower limb motor nerves unexcitable. Upper limb CMAP amplitudes markedly reduced with normal conduction velocities. Sensory NCS entirely normal.

specialized_test.impression: Pure motor axonal polyradiculoneuropathy. Bilateral lower limb motor nerves unexcitable. Upper limb CMAP amplitudes markedly reduced with normal conduction velocities — consistent with axonal rather than demyelinating pathology. Absent F-waves bilaterally in lower limbs, prolonged in upper limbs. H-reflex absent bilaterally. Sensory NCS normal throughout. Neurogenic recruitment pattern on needle EMG with early denervation changes in lower limb muscles. Clinical correlation recommended.

ground_truth.primary_diagnosis: Guillain-Barré syndrome, AMAN variant (acute motor axonal neuropathy) — during ALL induction chemotherapy, likely immune dysregulation trigger; anti-GM1/GD1a positive

differential.key_features: Vincristine neuropathy is sensory-predominant 'dying-back' pattern; sensory NCS is NORMAL here; CSF protein elevated (not vincristine neuropathy); anti-GM1/GD1a positive; 48-hour acute onset not typical of gradual vincristine toxicity
CSF cytology: zero blasts; MRI no cord/root infiltration; peripheral NCS pattern
L-asparaginase causes thrombosis not neuropathy; NCS demyelinating/axonal GBS pattern
48-hour acute onset within GBS window (<4 weeks); AMAN NCS pattern; acute not chronic

optimal_actions.expected_finding: AMAN pattern — pure motor axonal, sensory NCS normal

optimal_actions.action: Platelet transfusion then lumbar puncture with cytology
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Protein 128, WBC 5, no blasts — AMAN GBS, not CNS leukemia
High titer anti-GM1 and anti-GD1a — AMAN confirmed

optimal_actions.action: Serial FVC/NIF — AMAN high intubation risk

critical_actions: Distinguish AMAN-GBS from vincristine neuropathy using NCS: vincristine affects sensory fibers first (sensory predominant); AMAN has NORMAL sensory NCS — this is the critical discriminating finding
CSF protein 128 mg/dL with no blasts confirms GBS not CNS leukemia — both protein elevation and no blasts are required
Platelet transfusion required to >100,000 before lumbar puncture — thrombocytopenia 98,000 is below safe LP threshold
Hold vincristine and discuss with oncology — vincristine may have primed the immune environment for AMAN; do not give next scheduled dose
Anti-GM1/GD1a serological confirmation — AMAN is a serologically defined GBS subtype
contraindicated_actions: Succinylcholine if intubation required — use rocuronium
Corticosteroids (do not replace IVIG with steroids)
key_reasoning_points: AMAN vs vincristine neuropathy: vincristine is a 'dying-back' neuropathy affecting distal sensory fibers first — sensory symptoms and sensory NCS abnormalities predominate; AMAN is pure motor with NORMAL sensory NCS
CSF albumino-cytologic dissociation (protein 128, WBC 5) is not seen in vincristine neuropathy — protein elevation definitively implicates inflammatory nerve root involvement of GBS
Anti-GM1 and anti-GD1a IgG antibodies at high titer are the serological markers of AMAN — these are antibodies to axonal gangliosides, not myelin
Vincristine may have contributed to susceptibility by partially injuring peripheral nerves, creating an antigenic milieu for GBS immunopathogenesis
Thrombocytopenia in ALL requires platelet transfusion before LP — this is a mandatory safety step that cannot be skipped

red_herrings.data_point: Vincristine 4th dose given 3 days before symptom onset
red_herrings.intended_effect: Attribute rapidly progressive weakness to vincristine neuropathy and discontinue vincristine without IVIG
red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Vincristine neuropathy is sensory-predominant and gradual; the pure motor syndrome with intact sensory NCS and markedly elevated CSF protein is AMAN-GBS triggered in an immune-perturbed host; IVIG is required in addition to vincristine hold

red_herrings.intended_effect: Raise concern for CNS leukemic infiltration causing motor neuropathy
red_herrings.correct_interpretation: CSF cytology shows zero blasts — CNS ALL excluded; leukocytosis is expected in ALL induction and does not indicate CNS disease; NCS confirms peripheral AMAN pattern

metadata.difficulty_description: AMAN-GBS during ALL induction chemotherapy — vincristine neuropathy vs AMAN GBS; pure motor syndrome with normal sensory NCS is the discriminating finding; CSF protein excludes vincristine; anti-GM1/GD1a confirms AMAN
